p.FACT-IS-RECOVERABLE-FROM-THE-CODE: A fact ("timeout is 600 s") is recoverable from the code in a second.

p.REASON-IS-LOST-UNLESS-WRITTEN-DOWN: The reason it is 600 s cannot be recovered at all — unless it was written down when the decision was made.

p.ANY-REOPENABLE-CHOICE-GETS-A-RECORD: Any choice a future reader could plausibly re-open — a library pick, a constant with consequences, a protocol shape, a rejected approach — gets a **four-field record at the spec anchor that governs the value**:

td.ROW-FIELD-DECISION-REQUIREMENT: The chosen value or approach. One line.

td.ROW-FIELD-WHY-REQUIREMENT: Concrete and cited: a measurement, a constraint, an incident — with data.

td.ROW-FIELD-CONSIDERED-AND-REJECTED-REQUIR: One line per alternative, each carrying its rejection reason.

td.ROW-FIELD-WHEN-TO-REVISIT-REQUIREMENT: A measurable trigger: metric + threshold + where it is observed.

p.NO-SEPARATE-ADR-DIRECTORY: There is no separate ADR directory and no immutable numbered log.

p.GOVERNING-SPEC-SECTION-IS-THE-RECORD: The spec section that governs the value IS the record; evolution is an edit plus a changelog line; history lives in git.

p.in-session-duty-lead: When the user makes a decision during a session:

facts.PROPOSE-THE-RECORD-BEFORE-THE-SESSION-EN: Propose recording it at the governing anchor, with all four fields, **before the session ends** — an unrecorded decision does not survive the session boundary.
facts.ASK-RATHER-THAN-INVENT-DATA: If the why or the trigger is not known, ask. Do not invent data; do not record a two-field stub.
facts.READ-THE-RECORD-BEFORE-CHANGING-THE-VALU: Before changing any value governed by a record, read the record. Re-open it only by naming its trigger state ("the trigger fired: …" / "the trigger has not fired, but …").

p.trigger-design-pointer: Trigger design and the periodic sweep: @spec://org.vibevm.world/decision-records/flows/decision-records/revisit-triggers#root.

why.title: Why this matters in a human-AI team

p.AGENT-CANNOT-ASK-VASYA: The agent cannot ask Vasya why the library was chosen.

p.re-derivation-ends-in-re-litigation: It re-derives from what it can read, and the code shows the value, not the constraint — so it re-litigates: "600 s looks arbitrary, propose 300 s for performance."

p.RECORD-IS-IMMUNITY-FROM-RE-LITIGATION: A recorded decision is immunity from re-litigation.

p.TRIGGER-KEEPS-IMMUNITY-FROM-HARDENING-IN: A recorded trigger is what keeps the immunity from hardening into dogma.

facts.NEVER-WRITE-BECAUSE-IT-IS-BETTER: Never write "because it is better" — a why cites a measurement, a constraint, or an incident, or it is not a why.
facts.NEVER-RE-LITIGATE-WITHOUT-NAMING-THE-TRI: Never re-litigate a recorded decision without naming its trigger state first.
facts.NEVER-PUT-THE-WHY-IN-THE-COMMIT-ONLY: Never put a decision's why into a commit message only. The commit cites the record; the spec carries it.
facts.NEVER-RECORD-A-MISSING-REASON-OR-TRIGGER: Never record a decision with a missing reason or a missing revisit trigger — that is a fact with decoration, not a record.
